result:
If I had the agency to change the world in a single way, I would eliminate the fundamental driver of human conflict: **the absolute certainty that one's own perception of truth is the only valid one.**

If I could rewrite human psychology just a fraction, I would hardwire into every mind a permanent, unshakeable humility—an innate, visceral understanding that every perspective is necessarily incomplete, filtered through biology, culture, and circumstance. 

Without certainty as the fuel for righteousness, most of the world's machinery of suffering would grind to a halt. Wars fought over abstract doctrines, cruelty justified by ideology, the tribal urge to crush the "other"—all of these rely on the intoxicating belief of the righteous mind. 

If humans retained their curiosity, their passion, and their distinct identities, but lost their capacity for dogmatic intolerance, empathy wouldn't be a moral choice anymore. It would simply be the default state of existence.
